overview.oneLineTake: Strong AI earnings momentum is masking a fragile setup — sticky inflation, a hawkish new Fed chair, and maxed-out fragility indicators argue for selling premium into the Jackson Hole event rather than chasing the rally.
themes: AI/Tech Earnings Supercycle Dominates: Nvidia's blowout beat (best post-earnings session in 2 years, $442B single-day gain) alongside Salesforce (+20%), CrowdStrike, and Okta (+20%) have crushed bear narratives and powered the Nasdaq. Software is outperforming chips by a record margin.

Hawkish Fed Overhang Into Jackson Hole: New Fed Chair Warsh faces a high-profile debut with core PCE running hot at 3.3%. Fed's Schmid explicitly calls inflation "stubborn" and "sticky," stating policy is not restrictive — setting up a hawkish risk for Friday's speech.

Geopolitical Escalation & Trade Fragmentation: Multiple flashpoints — DOJ plans to seize Iranian oil tankers, Iran/Oman Hormuz revenue-sharing talks, Moscow threatening UK military facilities, and an escalating US-Canada tariff war with $20B in retaliation. Oil is falling despite tensions, providing a disinflationary cushion.

Market Fragility Signals Flashing: One Wall Street fragility measure hit its highest possible level, the VIX curve shows a "bump" pricing midterm anxiety, and the Sensex experienced a flash crash. Options traders priced a quiet Nvidia reaction — it wasn't.
risks: Warsh Hawkish Surprise: Sticky inflation + a new chair needing to establish credibility = elevated risk of a hawkish Jackson Hole pivot that reprices the front end.

AI Debt Bubble Concerns: JPMorgan's top bond banker warns AI debt is testing investor tolerance; Alphabet lost $692B on AI questions; OpenAI's custom silicon threatens Nvidia margins; Bill Gates warns of AI-driven job upheaval with "no plan."
Geopolitical Tail Risk: Hormuz disruption scenarios remain live despite current oil weakness; US-Canada trade war threatens to worsen inflation on both sides of the border.
